methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a reasonable multicenter observational design (N=410 across 24 Spanish hospitals, January 2022 to June 2025) with centralized HER2DX testing and central pathology review for TIL/TLS/TIME, which strengthens cross-site comparability. However, HER2 IHC, HR, and Ki67 were determined locally (acknowledged as a limitation), introducing information bias into one of the key comparisons. No a priori power calculation is reported, inclusion into the pCR substudy (250/410) risks selection bias that is not formally addressed, and the many pairwise comparisons across three scores by eight features are not corrected for multiplicity. Statistical methods (t/ANOVA/Mann-Whitney, chi-square/Fisher, Pearson, logistic regression with P<0.10 variable selection) are adequate and effect sizes with CIs are reported, but missing-data handling, model diagnostics, and sensitivity analyses are not described, and the multivariable pCR model's variable selection strategy is non-pre-specified.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a prospectively accrued, real-world multicenter cohort with central biomarker testing analyzed cross-sectionally against pathology, with a logistic regression against pCR in a subset, corresponding to Oxford LoE 2b (individual cohort/biomarker-correlative study). The clinical question is relevant: HER2DX is positioned to guide (de)escalation in early HER2+ breast cancer, and the pCR score remained the only independent multivariable predictor of pCR (OR 1.77; 95% CI 1.08-2.97) alongside associations with TIL, TLS, and immune spatial pattern. However, outcomes are limited to pCR (a surrogate) with no survival follow-up in this analysis, and the paper largely confirms expected biological associations of an already-validated assay rather than altering standards of care, so clinical impact is incremental supportive evidence.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is the appropriate standard because the manuscript evaluates a prognostic/predictive genomic biomarker (HER2DX) against pathology and pCR. The paper reports eligibility, assay provenance, pre-defined cutoffs, central vs. local assessment, and multivariable modeling, satisfying several REMARK items, but omissions include a formal patient-flow diagram, explicit handling of missing covariate data, pre-specified vs. exploratory analysis labeling, and a REMARK-style enumeration of candidate variables. No data-sharing statement, repository, analytical code, or protocol registration is apparent in the blinded text; only the R version is given, so reproducibility posture is weak.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is primarily empirical/populational: the authors frame this as the first comprehensive, directly comparative characterization of HER2DX pCR, risk, and ERBB2 scores against a broad panel of histopathologic and immune-microenvironment features in a real-world cohort. HER2DX itself is already analytically and clinically validated (refs 6-19) and prior work (ref 20) explored similar associations, so the conceptual and methodological novelty is modest. The main incremental contributions are the simultaneous side-by-side comparison of all three scores against eight features and the inclusion of TLS and TIME spatial patterns, which situates this as a meaningful but incremental extension rather than a field-defining advance.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written, logically organized (introduction frames the gap, methods are structured by assay/pathology/statistics, results follow the three HER2DX scores, discussion contextualizes with trial data), and the abstract is quantitatively grounded and faithful to the main findings. Figure captions are informative and self-explanatory, and tables are referenced where expected. Minor issues include some discussion sections that over-recapitulate validation of HER2DX (verging on promotional) and one typographic slip ('less biological variability then the pCR'), but overall the writing is publication-quality.

key_strengths: Large (N=410), prospectively accrued, 24-center real-world Spanish cohort with centralized HER2DX testing and central pathology review for TIL/TLS/TIME
Comprehensive, directly comparative evaluation of all three HER2DX scores against eight histopathologic and immune features, including TLS and spatial immune patterns

HER2DX pCR score remained the only independent predictor of pCR in multivariable analysis (OR 1.77; 95% CI 1.08-2.97; P=0.030), with biologically coherent correlations (IGG-TIL r=0.59; luminal-pCR r=-0.83)
Clear writing, strong contextualization against ATEMPT, APT, RESPECT, PerELISA, PHERGain, SCAN-B, and CompassHER2 datasets
key_concerns: Local (not central) HER2 IHC, HR, and Ki67 scoring introduces information bias in a comparison that hinges on these very variables
No pre-specified power calculation, no correction for multiplicity across 3 scores x 8 features, and no formal handling of missing data or selection bias in the 250/410 pCR subset
No data-availability statement, no code, no protocol registration apparent; REMARK items such as a patient-flow diagram and pre-specification of analyses are not clearly addressed
Novelty is incremental: the assay is validated, prior work (ref 20) already linked HER2DX modules to immune pathology, and this paper mostly confirms expected biology
pCR is the only outcome examined; no recurrence/survival data to anchor the risk score clinically in this cohort
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically competent, well-written biomarker-correlative study in a large real-world HER2+ cohort that provides incremental but clinically coherent evidence supporting HER2DX; strong enough for a tier-2 translational oncology venue with minor revisions (multiplicity, flow diagram, data-sharing, pre-specification) but lacks the novelty, survival endpoints, and reporting rigor needed for tier 1.
